scope: United States introductory issue narratives, measured 2020–2024 ACS ZCTA conditions on voluntary ZIP selection, and nonpartisan assistance resources. The ACS measurements do not identify a particular politician, household or causal policy result.

geography.purpose: Postal place label only. Nearby ZIP and matching ZCTA need not be identical; ACS statistics are shown with their source's ZCTA geographic code.
geography.privacy: Only on user submission, the chosen ZIP is sent by the browser to Zippopotam.us for an approximate postal place and Census Reporter for ACS ZCTA measures. Power Atlas does not record the value, retain it in localStorage or append it to the URL. Third parties have their own data policies.

issues.title: Housing
issues.question: Why does it cost so much to live here?
issues.description: Rent and housing prices reflect local supply, income, financing, demand, property costs and public decisions.

levers.why: Zoning, permits and infrastructure affect where and how housing can be built.
levers.evidence: Relevant decision-making power, not evidence of a particular local price effect.

levers.actor: Landlords, banks and major property owners
levers.why: Financing, market competition, construction and operating expenses shape supply and asking prices.
levers.evidence: Potential mechanism; no specific owner blamed without a source-backed local record.

levers.why: Housing assistance, mortgage rules and budgets influence access for eligible residents.
levers.evidence: Program jurisdiction; benefits and availability must be checked.

resources.name: Independent housing counseling
resources.note: Find a HUD-approved counselor for renting, borrowing or foreclosure.

resources.name: Local planning and public hearings
resources.note: Find official zoning proposals, meeting agendas and ways to submit public comment.

policies: Housing supply and planning reforms: possible long-term supply benefits; infrastructure and construction constraints apply.
Rent protections or direct assistance: may help eligible residents; effects on supply, availability and cost vary.

issues.title: Groceries
issues.question: Why is the supermarket bill so high?
issues.description: Food costs involve agriculture, logistics, fuel, labor, competition and household circumstances.

levers.why: Supply networks and competition can affect retail prices and shopping options.
levers.evidence: Potential mechanism; this app does not have verified ZIP-level price data.

levers.why: Tariffs, agricultural supports, labor rules and trade affect different parts of food supply.
levers.evidence: Policies have mixed effects and should not be assigned a local price without evidence.

levers.why: Nutrition support may offset costs for eligible households.
levers.evidence: Programs operate under eligibility and funding rules.

resources.name: Check food assistance eligibility
resources.note: Find official SNAP and other food-support programs.

resources.name: Report suspected consumer deception
resources.note: Submit a report; enforcement and refunds are not guaranteed.

policies: Competition oversight: focuses on documented market practices, not an assumption that large companies caused local inflation.
Nutrition assistance: may relieve qualifying household costs; does not directly measure price changes.

issues.title: Utilities
issues.question: Why do electricity and heating bills change?
issues.description: Prices and reliability reflect fuel costs, infrastructure, regulation, usage and weather.

levers.why: Infrastructure, fuel purchases, generation mix and investment affect costs and reliability.
levers.evidence: Possible mechanisms, not household-specific billing findings.

levers.actor: State utility regulators and public utility boards
levers.why: May oversee rates, service and investment for regulated utilities.
levers.evidence: Actual authority varies by state and utility type.

levers.why: Efficiency, aid, grid and climate programs can influence options and costs.
levers.evidence: Eligibility and effect size vary.

resources.name: State electricity profiles
resources.note: State-level statistics, not your individual energy rate.

policies: Energy-efficiency improvements: may lower usage, but upfront costs and building constraints matter.
Rate and reliability oversight: balance affordability and infrastructure investment; rules differ by provider.

issues.title: Healthcare
issues.question: Why is care hard to afford or access?
issues.description: Insurance networks, premiums, provider capacity, medicines and government rules differ by location.

levers.why: Negotiated prices, service networks and market structure shape how care is delivered.
levers.evidence: The cause of any individual's bill requires plan and provider details.

levers.actor: State regulators and federal healthcare agencies
levers.why: Coverage rules, licensing, payments and public programs influence care options.
levers.evidence: Authority and policy eligibility vary.

levers.why: Supply, facilities, staffing and travel distance affect practical access.
levers.evidence: Provider directory listings are not proof of available appointments.

resources.name: Review health insurance options
resources.note: Check eligibility and official marketplace plans.

resources.name: Compare Medicare care providers
resources.note: Official provider comparison tools; not a guaranteed appointment.

policies: Coverage and affordability reforms: may change who pays and how much; budget and provider effects vary.
Provider competition and staffing programs: could affect access but need local provider data.

issues.title: Jobs & pay
issues.question: Why do wages and job opportunities differ here?
issues.description: Local industries, employers, skills, contracts and business conditions affect hiring and pay.

levers.why: Business strategy, capital decisions and competition influence hiring and compensation.
levers.evidence: No direct link from named investors to a ZIP's wage levels has been validated.

levers.why: Awarded work can affect employer demand, but contracts are not company profit or guaranteed local jobs.
levers.evidence: Power Atlas has exact-entity federal awards but no local workforce-benefit join.

levers.why: Worker protections, training and credentials shape the options available to residents.
levers.evidence: Program effects vary across jobs and locations.

resources.name: Find an American Job Center
resources.note: Publicly funded job-search and training support.

resources.name: See verified federal-contract evidence
resources.note: Original Treasury award series, without inventing local job impacts.

policies: Workforce training: can improve access where local demand exists, but placement outcomes differ.
Procurement and wage requirements: may affect covered jobs but are not proof of economy-wide pay increases.

issues.title: Schools & children
issues.question: What affects our schools and childcare?
issues.description: School funding, enrollment, district rules, staffing and access to early learning vary by community.

levers.why: Budgets, facilities, staffing and curriculum decisions may be made locally.
levers.evidence: A ZIP is not a verified district boundary; school assignment requires the official district.

levers.why: Funding formulas, standards and oversight can affect resources and requirements.
levers.evidence: Specific policy consequences require state and district records.

levers.why: Operating costs, availability and care-workforce wages can influence childcare options.
levers.evidence: No ZIP-level childcare fee dataset is integrated.

resources.name: Find official school profiles
resources.note: Public school listings; check your district for actual assignment.

resources.name: Find local government and school board contacts
resources.note: Review published school budgets, minutes and public comment procedures.

policies: Funding and educator workforce options: outcomes depend on district needs, implementation and available resources.
Childcare subsidies and capacity policies: can improve access for eligible families but availability differs locally.

issues.title: Getting around
issues.question: Why is getting to work so expensive or difficult?
issues.description: Transit networks, roads, housing location, vehicle costs and fuel affect transportation.

levers.why: Service frequencies, routes and funding influence available transport options.
levers.evidence: ZIP alone does not identify a rider's exact service route.

levers.why: Road maintenance, safety and infrastructure decisions influence accessibility and travel.
levers.evidence: The effect on an individual's commute has not been measured.

levers.why: Fuel costs, workplace location and land use can change the demand and cost of travel.
levers.evidence: Potential mechanism rather than established local causation.

resources.name: Find your local government services
resources.note: Search transportation and infrastructure service providers.

resources.name: Explore federal transit programs
resources.note: Funding policy source, not live travel directions.

policies: Transit investment: may improve access, but costs and ridership vary.
Road and safety projects: depend on maintenance funding, land use and local priorities.

issues.title: Taxes & local services
issues.question: Where do taxes go—and what comes back?
issues.description: Public budgets fund schools, infrastructure, safety, benefits and other services under different layers of government.

levers.why: Adopt revenue and spending rules for many everyday services.
levers.evidence: ZIP does not establish a specific county, city or school tax bill.

levers.why: Disburse assistance and contract payments to verified recipients.
levers.evidence: An obligation is not cash received and does not identify household benefits.

levers.why: Procurement and enforcement influence how funds are allocated and monitored.
levers.evidence: A business award alone is not proof of favoritism.

resources.name: Inspect federal spending
resources.note: Compare awarded funds; scope and dates matter.

resources.name: Find public budget and meeting records
resources.note: Look up applicable officials and review local meeting agendas.

policies: Budget transparency and oversight: improves visibility but does not guarantee lower taxes.
Program and procurement redesign: may affect costs and outcomes; evaluations should compare service quality.

issues.title: Your voice
issues.question: Whose decisions shape the rules I live under?
issues.description: Electoral boundaries, elections, party coalitions, funding, lawmaking, judges and oversight shape representation.

levers.why: They administer and enact rules within judicial and constitutional constraints.
levers.evidence: State voting laws and current officials must be verified using official jurisdiction-specific sources.

levers.actor: Campaign committees, donors and advocacy groups
levers.why: They report some forms of political funding, lobbying and advocacy under different disclosure rules.
levers.evidence: Financial connections do not independently demonstrate improper influence or a vote change.

levers.why: Review legal disputes and enforce rules when they have jurisdiction.
levers.evidence: A case filing or appointment does not itself show wrongdoing.

resources.name: Find your serving U.S. representative
resources.note: A full street address may be needed where a ZIP crosses districts.

resources.name: Find officials and public contacts
resources.note: Government directory; verify current office holders and meeting procedures.

resources.name: Explore nonpartisan civic reform ideas
resources.note: Current rules and proposed changes are labeled separately.

policies: Political funding disclosure: improves public information but must protect lawful expression and privacy.
Small-donor programs, electoral procedures and independent oversight: effects, costs and legal feasibility differ by jurisdiction.

limitations: The local ZIP lookup is a third-party postal lookup, not a verified government jurisdiction lookup.

Census Reporter exposes source-backed, historical ZCTA ACS measures for all nine issues; no 2026 individual bills, store prices, school assignment or causal policy impact is estimated without specific source data.
Each deep-research record is shown according to its own publication status and gaps. It does not establish effects on the selected ZIP.
The interactive experience is not personal legal, medical or financial advice.
